messages:
elaine: FYI MAPBOX is seeing repeated 504s from hosted inference since ~10:40 UTC. Customer reports p95 tail timeouts and a bunch of request retries. Can we triage?
deploy-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-4823 — gateway 504 spikes (auto-alert).
raj: Got it. Any tenant id / request ids? Which region?
elaine: tenant=mapbox-prod, region=us-west2. Sample gateway id: gw-84f2. Logs show queue depth hitting 6000 and batchers backing up. Paste of recent lines:
```
2024-06-12T10:41:03Z gateway gw-84f2 INFO enqueue request tenant=mapbox-prod size=128
2024-06-12T10:41:04Z batcher btr-12 WARN backlog=3120 kv_cache_hits=0 inflight=1024
2024-06-12T10:41:05Z gateway gw-84f2 ERROR dispatch timeout after 30s request_id=abc123 http_status=504
```
raj: That backlog number is brutal. Looks like continuous-batcher is spinning up but can't keep up due to many small, short requests — continuous batching overhead + KV cache churn. Any recent customer config changes?
lisa: Mapbox changed from one large streaming request to many short non-stream requests in their update at 10:30 UTC. They said they rolled enabling "tile-metadata-sync" which fires thousands of tiny prompt calls.
samir: OK, likely workload change + queue depth hit. Immediate mitigation options: 1) apply tenant-level throttling at gateway (safest), 2) route mapbox to smaller/faster model variant (cheap, lower latency), 3) increase per-tenant queue_depth/inflight but that risks OOM on batchers, 4) temporarily scale continuous-batcher pool faster or restart to clear stuck batches.
raj: I'm going to run a quick live check on batcher pods in us-west2. If we see many pods with high thread count we should throttle.
(raj ran: `kubectl get pods -n hosted-prod -l app=continuous-batcher,region=us-west2 -o wide`)
raj: Seeing 18 batcher pods, many at 95% CPU, queue length per pod ~350. KV cache miss rate up.
elaine: Customer is asking for a quick workaround to stop 504s. They can accept a slight QoL drop if it keeps service up.
samir: Step 1: apply tenant throttle at gateway to smooth ingress. Suggest set tenant_max_inflight=200 and tenant_rate_limit=250rps for mapbox-prod. Use routing API: `POST /admin/routing/tenants/mapbox-prod/limits {"max_inflight":200,"rps":250}`. That should reduce enqueue pressure.
raj: I'll apply that now.
(raj executed): `curl -X POST https://admin.api.internal/routing/tenants/mapbox-prod/limits -d '{"max_inflight":200,"rps":250}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer **REDACTED**'`
raj: Throttle applied. Monitoring...
elaine: Notified customer about temporary throttle and reasons. Ask them to run their job again slowly.
~5m later~
customer-support: MAPBOX reports 504 rate dropped by ~92%, p95 improved from 6.1s to 1.2s. They still see occasional 504s for long-tail requests.
samir: Good. Next steps: 1) rollout a model-variant fallback for mapbox-prod to `redwood-small-v2` to reduce per-request compute. 2) Tune continuous-batcher autoscaler: reduce scale_cooldown and add cpu-based scaling for us-west2. 3) Postmortem + suggested client-side rate shaping.
raj: I'll open a scaling PR for batcher ASG and a runtime tweak: lower batcher.max_batch_latency from 50ms -> 30ms for short-request workloads. Also will add a metric alert for tenant enqueue spikes > 1000 for 1m.
elaine: Customer asked for ETA on permanent fix. We estimated changes (throttle + fallback) keep them safe; autoscaler & param tweaks will take ~2-4 hours to test and deploy. They asked for a postmortem once done.
lisa: I'll own customer comms and follow up with a runbook and recommended client throttling pattern.
elaine: Thanks all — leaving this thread open for the postmortem. :thumbsup:
